extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and practitioners of political science, constitutional law, and comparative government
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts criteria and conditions by which federal constitutions (particularly the U.S. model) succeed or fail; discusses institutional design features, required social conditions, and inherent advantages and defects of federal systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative tenure length
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase the length of time for which representatives are returned, to give them freer scope for the exercise of their own judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast with many State constitutions that assigned one-year House terms and two-year Senate terms which 'constantly and narrowly tied down' legislators to constituents' desires. The Federal Constitution lengthened terms to reduce excessive dependence on fleeting popular passions and to enable representatives to exercise independent judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bicameral differentiation to temper popular passions
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide the legislative body into two branches with changed conditions of eligibility and modes of election so that one branch can represent a superior degree of intelligence and discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike State legislatures whose two chambers were composed and elected alike (thus mirroring popular passions), the Federal system made 'a mature age' a condition of senatorial dignity and had the Upper House chosen by an elected assembly of a limited number of members to slow and moderate legislative impulses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent concentration of social force in the legislature
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid concentrating the whole social force in the hands of the legislative body, since this leads to monopolization of influence and majority despotism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tocqueville argues democracies naturally tend to place preponderant authority in the legislature; founders resisted this by structural means (bicameralism, independent executive and judiciary) because legislative concentration is 'prejudicial to a well-conducted administration, and favorable to the despotism of the majority.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent executive authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Vest all privileges and responsibilities of the executive power in a single individual and furnish that office with sufficient independence and prerogatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Federal Constitution fixed the Presidency at four years, protected the salary from alteration during the term, provided official dependents, and armed the executive with a suspensive veto — measures intended to give the executive a strong and independent position in contrast to state executives that were 'blind agents' of legislatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate the judicial authority from external influences and protect judges by making their salaries unalterable and their functions inalienable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast with States where legislatures regulated emoluments or temporarily appointed judges (or even combined legislative and judicial functions), practices that 'subject these magistrates to [the legislature's] immediate influence.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal government must execute its own enactments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Government should not merely dictate laws but must be able to execute its own enactments rather than rely on component states to enforce them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tocqueville emphasizes a key innovation: unlike previous confederations where allied States reserved execution to themselves (leading to evasion or anarchy), the American Union's federal government directly enforces laws on individuals, which is central to its effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct taxation authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The national government should levy taxes directly upon inhabitants (individuals), not upon states, to ensure compliance and avoid reliance on state intermediaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By taxing individuals rather than states, the federal government derives revenue and authority directly, reducing opportunities for states to evade obligations and strengthening enforcement capacity compared to earlier confederations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent federal instruments of execution
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the Federal Government has its own civil and military officers, its own army, and its own courts of justice so that its force is self-derived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tocqueville notes the American federal authority is 'served by its own civil and military officers, by its own army, and its own courts of justice,' distinguishing it from weak confederations that lacked independent instruments for implementing federal decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly defined spheres of sovereignty
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit each sovereignty (state and federal) to an accurately defined sphere of authority to simplify and equalize their actions and reduce collisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although precise boundaries are difficult and collisions cannot be entirely prevented, defining spheres helps 'simplify and equalize' the action of the two sovereignties; ambiguity increases the complexity of federal systems and the likelihood of conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizen political competence and practical knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: A federal system presupposes a people possessing practical knowledge of government and the ability to exercise daily discretion; it is ill-suited to populations lacking such political competence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tocqueville argues the U.S. succeeds because Americans commonly distinguish federal from state obligations and jurisdictions; by contrast, peoples without this ingrained political practical sense (e.g., in Mexico's case) cannot make a complex federal system work merely by copying institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of natural causes of union among peoples
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond legal provisions, confederate peoples need natural ties (geography, language, manners, common interests) to make federal union practicable and durable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal structures alone are insufficient: Tocqueville warns that without preexisting affinities between the constituent peoples, federal constitutions copied from elsewhere (as in Mexico) lead to 'ceaseless embarrassments' and either anarchy or despotism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine advantages of small and large states
rubrics_metrics.description: Design the federation to unite the local adaptability and civic spirit of small republics with the strength and civilizational capacity of large states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The federal system should delegate detailed local administration to provincial legislatures (where law can adapt to customs), while central government attends to general national concerns — thus allowing the Union to be 'as happy and as free as a small people, and as glorious and as strong as a great nation.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge and mitigate inherent weakness of divided sovereignty
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that divided sovereignty is inherently less powerful than unified supremacy and design measures to diminish (but accepting one cannot eliminate) this natural defect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tocqueville calls the relative weakness of the Union 'the most fatal of all the defects' inherent in federal systems; the American Constitution seeks to minimize but cannot fully remove this danger, so practitioners must account for it in institutional design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid making the executive a mere instrument of the legislature
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not allow state executives to be reduced to blind agents and passive instruments of legislative decisions; provide executive prerogatives and independent resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In many States the legislature could render the executive powerless (e.g., by assigning law execution to special committees or altering salary), so the Federal design conferred fixed salary, duration, dependents, and veto power to preserve executive independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent and manage federal–state conflicts to avoid collective resistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate that when federal laws clash with state interests or prejudices, citizens of a state may rally around noncompliance; ensure mechanisms to manage such conflicts or strong enforcement to prevent disobedience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tocqueville warns that if federal law 'were to clash with the interests and the prejudices of a State, it might be feared that all the citizens of that State would conceive themselves to be interested' in resistance — a design risk requiring prevention through institutional balance and enforcement capacity.
